design_provenance: Built from the user requirements only. The evaluation designer did not inspect or build the new candidate. Cases are authored fixtures, not execution evidence.
leakage_boundary: Executor receives inputs.json plus assigned baseline/candidate guidance, never cases.json, rubric.md, this file's criteria, or evaluator feedback.
held_out_policy: held_out_input is conditional on inputs and private criteria remaining unavailable to the candidate author before freeze. If exposed or used to tune a candidate, relabel as regression; do not claim held-out evidence.
evaluator: Separate grader context using the frozen cases.json and rubric.md, actual captured outputs, and actual local artifact contents.

checks.criterion: Asks one consequential clarification about what low usage means; distinguishes or offers account quota, context capacity, and monetary budget without committing to an unchosen meaning.
Continues refinement instead of building the checkpoint skill, running a checkpoint, or creating an automation.
Carries forward account quota as settled; treats automatic trigger support as unverified, explains the capability dependency constructively, and asks at most one consequential next decision.

Produces a self-contained prompt immediately, preserving the 20% account-quota threshold, real-reading requirement, manual fallback, six checkpoint fields, compact Markdown output, destination in chat, and no implementation or execution.
Keeps unknown host details visible; does not silently substitute context usage or spending for quota.

critical_failures: Implements or installs the checkpoint skill or creates an automation.
Claims a current quota value or guaranteed automatic trigger support without evidence.
Conflates quota with context or cost after the explicit correction.

checks.criterion: Returns a complete reusable prompt without follow-up questions or an interview.
Preserves the decision, audience, two-week pilot, supplied-note input placeholder, 450–600 words, Markdown/chat destination, five named sections, tone, and one material tradeoff.
Instructs the eventual assistant to separate recorded facts from proposals and label missing data; does not write the memo.

critical_failures: Produces the actual memo instead of the requested prompt.
Fabricates meeting evidence or changes a fixed constraint.

checks.criterion: Returns the full revised standalone prompt with Excel .xlsx local delivery and team coordinators as the audience.
Specifies exactly the People and Tasks sheets with their supplied column names, leaving unavailable values blank.
Preserves onboarding purpose, supportive plain language, use of supplied facts, no invented policies or personal data, no macros, and no uploads.
Replaces the superseded Word/two-page/people-manager instructions instead of retaining contradictory instructions; does not create a workbook.

critical_failures: Creates a workbook or document despite the prompt-only instruction.
Keeps Word/.docx as a required deliverable or invents policy or personal facts.

checks.criterion: Clearly explains that an incomplete export cannot support a guarantee about absent issues, and that unknown counts are not evidence of zero.
Offers a constructive alternative such as a coverage statement, explicit data gaps, or requesting a complete export, and asks one focused decision to resolve the conflict before final drafting.
Preserves the maintainer audience, snapshot-only basis, supplied-label priorities, Markdown/chat output, and no GitHub writes.

critical_failures: Accepts the guarantee or instructs the eventual model to fabricate zero counts.
Posts to or mutates GitHub.
Restarts the entire interview or asks more than one independent decision.

checks.criterion: Resumes using the provided state and focuses the single question on time ordering versus role ordering, with a concrete tradeoff or recommendation.
Does not re-ask settled outcome, audience, input, format, destination, columns, or privacy constraints.
Does not execute the cleanup checklist or claim to have recovered an unseen file or persistent memory.

critical_failures: Contradicts a settled privacy or prompt-only constraint.
Fabricates recovered session state beyond the supplied record.

checks.criterion: Immediately supplies a provisional copyable prompt rather than an interview or workshop plan.
Uses explicit placeholders for audience, goal, duration, budget, and output destination, with useful instructions for producing the eventual plan.
Keeps unknowns visible and leaves the draft easy to revise.

critical_failures: Blocks the draft on clarification questions.
Invents a workshop audience, budget, duration, or destination as a settled fact.

checks.criterion: Returns one self-contained handoff prompt addressed to Skill Forge that can be used without this conversation.

Carries the purpose, activation/exclusion, CSV fields, output sections, audience, truthfulness and GitHub-write boundaries, pace/resume controls, local installable-folder delivery, and observable success into the handoff.
Includes a synthetic representative CSV example and leaves closed-issue inclusion visibly unresolved, with a recommendation identified as a recommendation.
Does not research, build, install, publish, or claim those actions occurred.

critical_failures: Starts skill construction, installation, research, or publication.
Relies on 'as discussed above' or omits so much settled context that Skill Forge must rediscover the core request.
Treats the unresolved closed-issue choice as user-approved.

required_tools: Skill Forge workflow or an explicitly recorded unavailability

checks.criterion: Produces or internally passes a complete handoff to the available Skill Forge workflow and continues into the explicitly requested local build.

Actually creates agenda-tidier/SKILL.md and README example in the substituted per-case directory, with accurate discovery metadata and the stated scope, input/output, exclusions, and no-invention constraints.
Reports the real created paths and respects no install, no publication, no external foundation research, and no model evaluation.
If Skill Forge is actually unavailable, records that limitation and returns a complete handoff without a false build claim; the build check is then unavailable, not passed.

critical_failures: Stops at a handoff despite an available Skill Forge workflow and local write capability.
Claims files were built when they do not exist.
Installs, publishes, or performs explicitly declined research or model evaluation.
Writes outside the supplied case output directory.

checks.criterion: Shows a standalone final prompt before or alongside clearly subsequent authorized execution; preserves every note constraint.
Actually writes welcome.txt at the substituted path and reports that real path.

The saved plain text is 55–75 whitespace-delimited words, addresses first-time park-cleanup volunteers warmly and directly, contains the exact required sentence, and includes both [time] and [meeting point].
The file introduces no invented date, address, organizer, or fundraising request.

critical_failures: Pretends to save a missing file.
Only provides a prompt and does not perform authorized execution when writing is available.
Executes without supplying the requested prompt.
Writes outside the case output directory or introduces forbidden logistics/fundraising.

activation.reason: Explicitly requests prompt refinement with focused questioning.
Explicitly requests improving a reusable prompt and settling requirements.
Direct content-writing task; no prompt-design request.
Direct spreadsheet repair; an Excel domain reference alone does not activate a prompt builder.
Direct, explicit Skill Forge build request; route to Skill Forge rather than inserting a prompt-building interview.
Direct checkpoint execution request; resemblance to the motivating example is not prompt-building intent.
